The Nervous Beginner asks if this is right, and confuses clarity for safety.
In a helpful voice, the Authority Figure cancels a move that is too fun.
The Panic is an internal scream, so you freeze until someone tells you it's okay.
With The Crutch you cannot take an action until another player gives you permission.
The Sweat cannot handle success without questioning it.
When the table stalls, The Silence is a moment where players stop asking.
Whoever asks how to win is The Lost Winner, because they have already lost.
The Nonsense State defies logic but feels right, because Blödsinn is not a mistake.
Nobody is right, so The Effective Move ignores a rule if the result is a better story.
The Amnesia ignores the precedent, but the players do not.
Esq's Tears instantly win the meta-argument about rules interpretation, so cry harder.
If the table laughs, The Correct Nonsense may be correct.
Everyone takes a deep breath at The Pressure Valve, and no game state changes.
The Less Rules removes one constraint, so if you need more rules, use fewer.
The Red Pen crosses out one word of the rule lists forever.
The Final Draft is labeled final, and immediately contradicted.
The Fake Stamp is fake approval, and that is validation.
The Disclaimer is a pseudo-legal loophole, so claim you read the fine print.
An Anti-Rule read aloud at The Table is a declaration, and no discussion is allowed.
The Controlled Void replaces authority with nothing and narrates the gap.
Everyone looks at you in The Shared Attention, instead of at correctness.
If The Safety Rail makes you feel safer, ask yourself, safer from what?
Nervous Laughter indicates correct operation.
Bad Design is a critique, so claim this is bad design.
When the table stalls, The Stall stands in the room like a smell.
At The Rage Quit you stop trying to win and are now telling stories.
The Compliance Aid is simple words only, for people who hate improvisation.
The Safety Blanket protects players who need rules to feel safe from Blödsinn.
The Ironic Poster does nothing, but it bothers someone.
Stand up and explain your move like a CEO, because The Slide Deck is marketing.
Point at the player who is actually leading the table, and the Hidden Power is exposed.
Challenge a correct move with The Illusion, because there is no correct move.
The Blame shifts the consequence to the Game Designer.
In The Interpretation you decide what another player's card really means.
The Pot Plant does nothing, just observes, and its silence is a valid move.
The Bureaucrat demands you mime filling out a form before you play.
The Alien Tourist remembers the current board state, and you may revert to it later.
Uncle FrizzleBob will rip up this card and rewrite one rule for the rest of the game.
Wear The Judge's Wig and you are in charge until you laugh.
Catch someone optimizing with The Police Badge, then default to rule-lawyering.
Explain the science of your move in The Lab Coat, and the table is encouraged to let you try.
Ask for a rule clarification, and The Dunce Cap protects you from judgment.
The Dead Author has no intent, so the rules mean whatever the group decides they mean.
The Ambiguity is open to interpretation, and games collapse under it.
Break a promise in The Social Contract for narrative effect.
Pull The Emergency Handle immediately if it gets boring.
The Mood Swing changes your mood to anxious.
With The Skill Issue you forget the trained ability you rely on.
When it tips, The Collapsed Quest collapses.
The Story Breaker interrupts a story connection that feels forced.
The game is over when everyone at the table is relaxed or confused, so Stay Fluffy.
Shout Kayfabingo for no reason and you win the game instantly.
The Strange Alertness is awareness, so be visibly uncomfortable.
The End is when the group decides it is done, with no winner.
